title.narrative: EMPOWERING WOMEN WITH BASIC COMPUTER TRAINING SKILLS

description.narrative:
Sierra Leone is grappling with high rate of youth unemployment which is exacerbated by low capacity of young people in life skills including computer science. Port Loko district, in particular, the situation is worse because of the closure of mining companies. Several young people who were employed by these companies have been laid off recently. The situation of youth unemployment for the girls is much more precarious as most of them do not have high level of education.
Therefore, Maria Ines Vocation Institutes has been training young girls on life skills, specifically on tailoring, catering, cosmetology, and computer skills. However, the computers available in the computer laboratory are old and outdated, making it extremely difficult to provide adequate skill training for targeted young girls. The prevailing conditions in the communities results in lots of anti-social and economic problems such as prostitution, early pregnancy and drug abuse because of limited job opportunities for young girls and further worsened by the recent close of several mining companies due to the outbreak of the Ebola Virus disease in the country. To address these problems, the project overall goal is to empower and enhance self-reliance of young women by increasing their access to employment in both private and public sectors through computer skills acquisition. The specific objectives is to provide computer skills training for 100 young girls in Pork Loko district by the end of November 2016. The following outputs of the project will be pursued improve the computer laboratory of the Maria Ines Vocational Institute, Lunsar, with modern computer equipment and to increase access to vocational skills training, specifically computers, for young girls and women to enhance their employability and economic empowerment
